note.text:
When we meet someone for the first time, we greet and introduce ourselves.
• Greet: “Good morning.” “Good afternoon.” “Good evening.” With friends: “Hello” or “Hi”.
• Introduce yourself: “My name is Bih. I am from Kumbo. I am in Form One.”
• Introduce another person: “This is my friend Ayuk.” “Mummy, meet Tabe, my classmate.”
• Reply: “Nice to meet you.” “Nice to meet you too.” “Pleased to meet you.”
• Ask: “What is your name?” “Where are you from?” “How are you?”
With an older person or a teacher, greet first, add “sir” or “madam”, and use “Good morning” rather than “Hi”.

worked_example.problem: On the first day of school, {a} meets a new classmate, {b}. {a} is with his friend {c}. What do they say?
steps: Give your name and one fact: {a}: “My name is {a}. I am from Mamfe.”
The other person greets back and gives her name: {b}: “Good morning, {a}. My name is {b}. I am from Kumbo.”
Introduce your friend: {a}: “{b}, this is my friend {c}.”
Reply politely: {b}: “Nice to meet you, {c}.” {c}: “Nice to meet you too.”
worked_example.answer: Greet → give your name → introduce the other person → reply politely.

cards.idea: To introduce yourself, greet first, then give your name and one or two facts about you.
example: “Good morning. My name is {name}. I am from {town}. I am in Form One.”

check.prompt: Which is the best way to introduce yourself to a new classmate?

right.text: “Hello, my name is {n}. I am from {t}.”

wrong.explain: Use full sentences: “My name is …”, “I am from …”.
“Goodbye” is for leaving, not for meeting someone.

wrong.text: “What is your name? Nice to meet you too.”
wrong.explain: Give your own name first; “Nice to meet you too” is a reply.
“Hey you!” is not polite. Greet and give your name first.

cards.idea: To introduce another person, say “This is …” and add who the person is.
example: {a}: “{b}, this is my cousin {c}. She is in Form One too.”

misconceptions.explain: To introduce someone, we say “This is …”, not “He is …”.
“It” is for things, not people. Say “This is …”.
“There is” tells that something exists. To introduce someone, say “This is …”.

cards.idea: When someone is introduced to you, answer politely and use the person's name.
example: {c}: “Nice to meet you, {b}.” {b}: “Nice to meet you too.”

cards.idea: Greet by the time of day: Good morning (before midday), Good afternoon (after midday), Good evening (in the evening). “Good night” is for leaving, not for greeting.
example: After school, at about four o'clock: “Good afternoon, sir.”

pick.right: Hello, Enow. My name is Mih.
pick.why: When someone tells you their name, greet them by name and give your own name.
The polite reply to “Nice to meet you” is “Nice to meet you too.”
“What is your name?” asks for a name: “My name is …”.
“Where are you from?” asks for a place: “I am from …”.

pick.right: I am fine, thank you. And you?
pick.why: “How are you?” asks how you feel: “I am fine, thank you.”

pick.right: Hello, Manyi. Nice to meet you.
pick.why: When someone is introduced to you, greet them by name and say “Nice to meet you.”

misconceptions.explain: Good morning is for the morning, before midday.
Good afternoon is for the time after midday until about five or six o'clock.
Good evening is for the evening.
Good night is said when leaving at night or before going to bed, not to greet someone.

questions.prompt: Tap the words in the right order.
Each line is a question and its answer. One answer does not fit its question. Which one?

right.text: “How are you?” — “I am fine, thank you.”
“Nice to meet you.” — “Nice to meet you too.”
“This is my friend {f}.” — “Hello, {f}. Nice to meet you.”

wrong.explain: The question asks for a name. The answer should be “My name is …”.
“How are you?” asks how you feel. The answer should be “I am fine, thank you.”

wrong.text: “Where are you from?” — “I am fine, thank you.”
wrong.explain: “Where are you from?” asks for a place. The answer should be “I am from …”.
The polite reply is “Nice to meet you too.”
